column1: What is the status of Lecture 6 in the course?
column2: It is the last formal lecture - everything after it is project work.

column1: What was the stated purpose of the first three weeks of SE761?
column2: To introduce you to agile so that you can get started within your teams.

column1: When does sprint 1 present, and in what form?
column2: Week 6, with each team presenting in pairs.

column1: When is the final SE761 presentation?
column2: Week 11.

column1: Roughly how long is the development window after the taught content?
column2: About eight weeks.

column1: What does the lecturer say about the mid-semester break?
column2: It is going to be very important, and working more during it will help.

column1: What is the lecturer's phrase about starting a project?
column2: A well started is half done - so work hard in the first few sprints.

column1: What is Assignment 3 in one sentence?
column2: Take your allocated project, decompose it into themes, take one theme, find a research paper on it, and write a reflection on what it teaches you about your project.

column1: What are Assignment 3's three learning outcomes?
column2: Go deeper into exploration of the project rationale through research literature; discover and demonstrate new insights around the topic area; and critically study the research literature to accumulate evidence for what you claim to understand.

column1: What is the real purpose of Assignment 3, beyond the marks?
column2: To let you present evidence to the Product Owner at the first meeting so they have more confidence in your team.

column1: Have you met the client by the time Assignment 3 is due?
column2: No - both A1 and A3 rationales are written before meeting the Product Owner.

column1: Why does the lecturer say Assignment 3 scores twice?
column2: Because it also contributes directly to the project work.

column1: What is Assignment 3 worth?
column2: 7% of the course, marked out of seven.

column1: What is Assignment 3's word limit and format?
column2: 800 to 900 words, in full paragraphs, submitted via the Canvas A3 quiz.

column1: How many topics does Assignment 3 cover, versus Assignment 1?
column2: Assignment 3 covers your one allocated project; Assignment 1 covered any three topics from the catalogue.

column1: What is the research requirement difference between A1 and A3?
column2: A1 explicitly required no literature review; A3 requires a real research paper, attached to the submission.

column1: Which A1 mistake stops being a mistake in A3?
column2: Mentioning the solution - A3 permits bringing in purpose, though not solution specifics.

column1: Which concept licenses talking about purpose in A3?
column2: L2-C03 - purpose links rationale to product, proportionally.

column1: What is the Gen AI position on Assignment 3?
column2: You may still use it, but limit it as much as possible because it is a reflection; there is still a declaration section.

column1: How do the Gen AI policies compare across A1, A2 and A3?
column2: A1 encouraged it and gave 2 marks for declaring; A2 forbids it for content; A3 permits but discourages it, with a declaration.

column1: What voice may Assignment 3 be written in?
column2: Personal language is permitted with professional tone; a more formal third-person perspective is also acceptable.

column1: How do you decompose a project for Assignment 3?
column2: Read the description for a major theme and its sub-themes, or multiple major themes, then divide them among team members.

column1: What is the stated reason for splitting a project by theme?
column2: To attack the problem description from different angles - a divide-and-conquer approach.

column1: Your eight-person team can only find three themes. What do you do?
column2: Distribute the three themes among members, with two or three members per theme - but each must work on a different paper.

column1: What is the binding constraint in theme allocation?
column2: One unique paper per person, not one theme per person.

column1: What two purposes does the different-paper rule serve?
column2: Avoiding duplicate work, and attacking the problem from multiple angles.

column1: Name the five themes the lecturer drew from the smart home AR project.
column2: AR interfaces for smart home control; gesture-based interaction in AR; quality aspects such as usability and accessibility in smart home UIs; gesture recognition technologies; and multi-device integration and universal interfaces.

column1: What pattern do the smart-home themes follow?
column2: Core technologies, then a quality attribute, then an enabling technology, then integration.

column1: Name the five steps of the Assignment 3 method.
column2: Break down core research themes; identify relevant databases; define search keywords and strings; select and summarise relevant papers; draft the rationale.

column1: Which database is sufficient on its own for Assignment 3?
column2: Google Scholar, because it returns papers from all the other databases.

column1: What do specialised databases add over Google Scholar?
column2: More papers or more relevant papers - better precision, not better coverage.

column1: Why must search strings be designed carefully?
column2: Because missing one word can return irrelevant material that is not obviously irrelevant, and can misguide you in the wrong direction.

column1: Why search plain Google as well as Google Scholar?
column2: Google tells you what applications already exist; Scholar tells you what is known in the research.

column1: How do specialised projects differ from general ones when searching?
column2: Specialised projects have more relevant research and fewer existing apps; general projects have more apps and possibly less research.

column1: What is the minimum length for a double-column research paper?
column2: Five pages.

column1: What is the minimum length for a single-column research paper?
column2: Eight pages.

column1: What is excluded from the paper page count?
column2: References, which are generally one to two pages, and any other substantial non-text pages.

column1: What venues are acceptable for the Assignment 3 paper?
column2: Conferences, journals, workshops or symposia.

column1: What is an idea paper, and why is it disqualified?
column2: A two- or three-page article that is too limited in providing relevant knowledge - Assignment 3 wants more detailed research articles.

column1: Can you use more than one paper for Assignment 3?
column2: Yes - one or more, depending on your wish or on whether your theme needs it.

column1: How is the research paper submitted?
column2: Attached as a PDF in a separate section of the Canvas quiz.

column1: How many questions must you answer in Assignment 3, and how are they marked?
column2: At least four, at one mark each, making four of the seven marks.

column1: Give the four example questions for Assignment 3.
column2: Why was this paper useful in relation to your project or theme; what would your client appreciate you understanding; was there anything that surprised you; and what new learning came out of it.

column1: Can you replace the example questions in Assignment 3?
column2: Yes - you may pick other questions or replace one or more of them.

column1: What is the rule about how you answer the Assignment 3 questions?
column2: Each answer must be relevant to both the paper you picked and your project - not answered in a general way.

column1: What do the remaining three Assignment 3 marks cover?
column2: Reflection quality, agility reflection, and writing style.

column1: What does reflection quality mean in the A3 rubric?
column2: Whether there was a high enough level of reflection, whether you demonstrated new insights from the attached research, and whether it relates to the project.

column1: What is the lecturer's advice on the 800 to 900 word range?
column2: Target 800 words, expect to end up somewhat over, and never go beyond 900.

column1: Do you need references in Assignment 3?
column2: No - the only reference is the actual paper you attach.

column1: What happens after every team member finishes their individual Assignment 3?
column2: The team meets, shares what each has learned, and collates it into a more in-depth project rationale.

column1: Is Assignment 3 individual or team work?
column2: Each member works independently, but the results are collated to benefit the team's overall work.

column1: What is the standard for any point you present to the Product Owner?
column2: Every point must have backing evidence.

column1: What should you do if research shows similar apps already exist?
column2: Be honest with the client - tell them what you found, note they may not know, and ask whether they still want to proceed or want changes to existing apps.

column1: What should you do if research suggests a requirement is not feasible?
column2: Raise it as a question with the client, based on the evidence.

column1: What should you do if the client's technical choice looks outdated?
column2: Research it - their understanding may be outdated, and you may find evidence for a better option, but you must find that evidence.

column1: What did the lecturer say about interpreting the client?
column2: Be very careful about what they say, but be able to interpret them correctly.

column1: How does Assignment 3 relate to says, wants and needs?
column2: Research is how you move from what the client says to what they need before you have even met them, and evidence is what makes that sayable.

column1: What technologies were given as an evidence example for gesture recognition?
column2: MediaPipe and CNNs.

column1: Name the standard sections of a research paper in order.
column2: Summary or abstract, introduction, literature review, research questions, then method and results.

column1: What does a paper's summary give you?
column2: The problem being solved, how it is addressed, how it is reported, the end result, and what can be inferred from the research.

column1: What is the literature review doing structurally?
column2: Telling a little story that connects the dots from earlier work up to the current research in the area.

column1: How does a paper frame its own contribution?
column2: The research in the area is ending at this point, and this is where we start from - then it proposes one or two research questions.

column1: Why is knowing paper structure useful for Assignment 3?
column2: The abstract answers "is this on my theme?" in seconds, and the literature review is a pre-built map of the theme that can point you to better papers.

column1: Which A1 idea does the research-gap framing resemble?
column2: The upside-down triangle - broad to specific - done with citations.
